name: canon
position_index_notes: Which physical camera/lens generation is installed. INCREMENT whenever the camera, lens or mounting changes — each index is a distinct calibration epoch (plate scale, pole, FOV, orientation, pedestal) that must NOT be mixed across the boundary. Stamped into every FITS as POSINDEX. Index 2 = Canon EOS 2000D, lens on MANUAL focus set BY EYE through the optical viewfinder at datum 'marker 0' (see capture.focus_notes).

1.label: eos1
1.notes: RETIRED 2026-08-10. First deliverables epoch: 30s ISO-1600 subs, fixed mount (stars TRAIL ~5-8 px/sub), focus nominally driven to LENS-DIAL d7. Superseded because astro-canon RETIRED the whole `d` apparatus — the dial was found to be tracking NOTHING (2026-08-08 sharpness split by capture PASS, not by d), so this epoch's V-curve/peak focus conclusions are WITHDRAWN. Only real data: the thin 8-frame 2026-08-08 'd7' subset used for pipeline bring-up. Do NOT mix with epoch 2.

2.label: eos2
2.notes: Current epoch. Same body/lens/mount as epoch 1 — the FOCUS MECHANISM changed: lens switched to MF and focused BY EYE through the optical viewfinder (datum 'marker 0'), nights run --no-focus so the ring is never driven, not even after a power cycle. Frame stems carry a null placeholder _d00 (NOT a dial position). Incremented deliberately (Peter, 2026-08-11) under the position_index rule: focus regime is a calibration boundary, so epoch-1 d7 frames and epoch-2 marker-0 frames are never co-solved. First night: 2026-08-10 (460 frames, 6.6 h, focus stable end-to-end). plate_scale/pole UNSOLVED — derot disabled until a clear-night trail-arc solve.

bayer_notes: Decoded from rawpy raw_pattern [[3,2],[0,1]] + color_desc 'RGBG' on a real CR2 (2026-08-09): the 2x2 CFA tile reads [[G,B],[R,G]] = GBRG. NOT RGGB — do not assume. Registered here directly (astro.process.bayer.SENSOR_RAW_FORMAT covers only the Pi sensors); pipeline reads cfg.bayer.
resolution_notes: raw.raw_image_visible shape (4015 rows x 6020 cols), uint16 14-bit (white_level 16383). This is the visible sensor area rawpy exposes, larger than the nominal 6000x4000 due to masked/border columns.

capture.gain_from_iso_note: The EOS has no libcamera GAIN; the pipeline's GAIN header is set = ISO/100 (1600 -> 16.0) as the documented convention, so brightness-per-(EXPTIME*GAIN) is comparable in spirit to the Pi cameras. It is NOT a calibrated e-/ADU gain; it is a consistent normalisation constant. Change it here and re-derive pedestal/scs if ISO changes.
capture.focus_notes: Focus is set BY EYE through the optical VIEWFINDER with the lens on MANUAL — datum 'marker 0' (astro-canon, 2026-08-10). Nights run --no-focus: the ring is never racked or driven, not even after a power cycle (a rail drop cannot move a mechanical ring). The `d` apparatus is RETIRED, not merely pinned: by-eye focus beat every driven method outright (edge/std 0.151 vs 0.055 for the best metric-guided bracket, 0.035 for the all-day d-schedule), and `d` was found to be tracking NOTHING — 2026-08-08 sharpness split by capture PASS, not by d — so the earlier V-curve/peak/'d7 is the focus' conclusions are WITHDRAWN. Frame stems still carry `_d00`: a NULL PLACEHOLDER, not a dial position. Consequence for delivery: never pass --only-d 7 to eos-cr2-to-fits (it would filter out every frame); run with no --only-d at all. Validated on 2026-08-10 — 460 frames over 6.6 h with median star FWHM 2.25-2.63 px from first frame to last.
capture.capture_notes: gphoto2 tethered capture on muppet via the eos-* tool lineage (eos-focus-tonight / eos-focus-cycle). Writes CR2 (+ boosted JPEG) to muppet's /mnt/bigstore/astro-data/eos-frames/<night>/ (pip sees it at /mnt/muppet/bigstore/eos-frames/<night>/) — capture MOVED there from the old ~/tmp/canon-focus-nightly/<night>/, which is still eos-cr2-to-fits's built-in default, so pass --src explicitly until that default is updated. Those CR2s are adapted to .fits.fz by eos-cr2-to-fits into frames_root for the nights pipeline. Stars TRAIL within a 30s sub (~5-8 px) — a short-trail fixed-mount camera, between a tracked stack and a full drift-scanner.

plate_scale_notes: UNSOLVED. No plate solve yet for the 2000D + lens. Derive from a clear-night trail-arc fit (same method as the Pi cameras) before trusting any angular measurement or enabling derot.
pole_prior_notes: UNSOLVED. Pole position in the 2000D frame is unknown (fixed mount, unmeasured aim). Derot is DISABLED until this is solved from real sky. nightly-cam must degrade gracefully (max.jpg + brightness + summary, no derot) when pole_prior_xy is null — verified during canon bring-up.
rotate_180_notes: No downstream rotation. DSLR raw is delivered in the sensor's native orientation; any sky-up convention is deferred to the (unsolved) pole/derot stage. Set false so the raw mosaic is stacked as-read.
pedestal_notes: PROVISIONAL. Reference for the brightness chart's log2(mean/pedestal) 'stops' axis. Set to 2048 as a first cut — just below the measured per-channel black level (~2046-2052 on a real CR2, 14-bit) — so a dark clear frame reads a small positive number of stops with footroom, mirroring the astrocam pedestal logic on the EOS's very different scale. MUST be re-derived from the first real dense marker-0 night's dark-sky frame-mean (2026-08-10) before the brightness chart / cloud verdict are trusted (the copied-from-astrocam risk the pedestal double-duty memory warns about — this axis also anchors sky_clear_max_stops).
frames_root_notes: Where the adapted .fits.fz frames live (eos-cr2-to-fits writes here; nightly-cam reads here). Resolved PER-HOST like the other cameras: default (~/canon-frames) is muppet's view (capture + adapter run on muppet); pip sees muppet's bigstore export at /mnt/muppet/bigstore/canon-frames. This is the ADAPTED FITS tree, NOT the raw CR2 dir (~/tmp/canon-focus-nightly/<night>/), which is the adapter's input.
night_layout_notes: YYYY-MM-DD/HH/HH-MM-SS.fits.fz (UTC hour dirs); night membership by DATE-OBS within the noon-rollover window. Chosen because the adapter can place each CR2 by its manifest t_utc directly, and night_output_dir(flat) drops derived artefacts in the night dir. Same layout as astrocam.
processing_notes: Split by dependency: the CR2->FITS ADAPTER (eos-cr2-to-fits) runs on muppet (needs rawpy + is where capture writes the CR2s); nightly-cam / publish-night-cam (FITS->deliverables, needs matplotlib) run on PIP, reading the adapted frames over NFS (/mnt/muppet/bigstore/canon-frames). Mirrors the drift-scan cameras processing on puppy off muppet's export. muppet has rawpy but not matplotlib; pip has matplotlib but not rawpy — neither host can do both halves, so the adapter/nightly-cam split is load-bearing, not incidental.
sky_clear_max_stops_notes: UNSET until measured. Dark-trough (10-min anchor) stops above which the night is called cloudy. Cannot be copied from astrocam — the EOS pedestal axis and LP response differ. Derive from the first real dense marker-0 nights (clear vs cloudy anchors) exactly as astrocam's was, THEN set a value with margin. Until set, either treat all nights as stackable (no cloud gate) or gate on a coarse brightness cut — decide during bring-up.
reference_nights_notes: Populate with a known dark/clear marker-0 baseline once one is captured.
